utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody, especially to you, Mr. Elderkin, the first time we see you in the courtroom this year, and we wish you a happy and successful year. I think the next witness is ready. We go into closed session for a moment to enable the witness to enter the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Good morning, sir. Welcome to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would you please read aloud the affirmation on the card which is shown to you now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please sits down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: As you know, there are still protective measures in place for you. You will be addressed by a pseudonym and nobody will recognise you on the screen because of face distortion. Mr. Elderkin has questions for you and is commencing his examination-in-chief. Mr. Elderkin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And witness, good morning to you. As you know, my name is Rupert Elderkin and I will be asking you a few questions this morning. If there is anything that I ask you that is unclear, please let me know and I will try to rephrase my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Can I ask first to have 65 ter number 7167 on the screen? And this shouldn't be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Sir, without telling us your name, are you the person named on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I request that the pseudonym sheet be admitted now under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P1761 and admitted under seal, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall having testified here in The Hague in the Krstic trial in April 2000?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Was your testimony truthful?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And have you had the opportunity to review your testimony in the past few days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Having reviewed your testimony, does it fairly and accurately reflect what you would say if you were to be examined here today and asked the same questions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, I move to have the witness's testimony from the Krstic trial admitted, and that's 65 ter number 1553. And in addition, 65 ter numbers 1207 and 1227 were admitted through the witness in the Krstic trial, and I'd also ask for their admission now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please clarify, the transcript of the 14th of April, that was in the Popovic case or in the Krstic trial?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: It was in the Krstic trial, Your Honour. The witness last testified before this Tribunal in Krstic and his testimony was subsequently admitted in Popovic and also I think in Blagojevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And they are all public documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And the transcript is a public document, indeed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: They will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1553 shall be assigned Exhibit P1762. 65 ter document 1207 shall be assigned Exhibit P1763. 65 ter document 1227 shall be assigned Exhibit P1764. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours for the record, one additional exhibit was used with the witness during his Krstic testimony, and that has already been admitted in this trial as Exhibit P262. I'd like now to read a summary of the witness's Krstic testimony. The witness is a Muslim by faith. On the 11th of July 1995, he was living with his family in the village of Suceska in Srebrenica. That day, his family went to Potocari but he went to Jaglici as he was afraid of being killed by Serb soldiers. There were around 10 to 15.000 people at Jaglici who decided to head for Tuzla. The witness set off on the afternoon of the 12th of July. He spent the night in the woods and was captured near Nova Kasaba at around 7.00 a.m. on the 13th of July. He was taken to the elementary school in Kasaba which was being used as a barracks. Around 2.00 p.m., the captured Muslims at the school were taken to a nearby football pitch. There were around 1.500 to 2.000 men sitting in rows surrounded by armed Serb soldiers. While the witness was at the football pitch, more Muslim men were arriving from the direction of Konjevic Polje. The Serb soldiers said that General Mladic would come and he arrived and made a speech saying that the men would all be exchanged. Mladic also ordered the soldiers to make a list of the prisoners. While Mladic was present, the soldiers killed a prisoner. After the list was made, Mladic left towards Konjevic Polje. In the late afternoon, buses came and drove the prisoners towards Bratunac. Near Sandici, the witness saw a group of men surrounded by Serb soldiers. Further on, near Kravica, the witness saw a building with four or five dead bodies at the central entrance and he heard shooting from behind the building. The bus stopped for the night in Bratunac. The witness heard shooting throughout the night and four or five people were taken off the bus and never came back. The next day, 14th of July, the prisoners remained on the bus. They were not given any water and people were fainting because of the heat. A soldier arrived and told the prisoners they were going to be exchanged. The bus drove north to Pilica. At the school there, the soldiers ordered the prisoners into the school gymnasium which was already crowded. The witness volunteered to get water. While he was outside, he heard a bus approaching and then there was the sound of people crying for help, then shooting and the guard ordered the men getting water back into the gym. Two or three men died during the night from lack of air in the overcrowded gym. On the 15th of July, Serb soldiers robbed the men in the gym and threatened to kill them if they did not hand over 10.000 German marks but they did not have the money. During the night, the 15th of July, men were taken out of the gym and some didn't come back. On the morning of the 16th of July, a Serb soldier said, "Let all the young men leave the gym. One by one, because they will be exchanged." The witness's hands were tied, then he went outside and got on to a bus. The bus drove to a meadow where there were many dead bodies. The soldiers took groups of men from the buses and shot them. As the witness was getting off the bus, the Serb soldiers asked if anyone had any relatives abroad so that they could send money for exchange. And some people spoke up and were singled out. The witness was taken to the meadow with the bodies. Serb soldiers there opened fire with automatic rifles and a machine-gun. Then there was an order to shoot people individually. The witness was shot in the back but was only scratched. The soldiers asked if anyone was wounded and said they would be bandaged. Those who spoke up were finished off. More groups of prisoners were brought to the meadow and were killed. That evening, a vehicle arrived and unloaded more bodies at the site. The witness spent the night in the killing field and the next day hid under a bridge. From his hiding place, he heard the sounds of machines working all day. He met an older man and they escaped together. They met a third man but he eventually got lost. The witness and the older man turned themselves in when they became exhausted. They were given food and drink and were taken to Karakaj in a minibus. The witness was taken on to the Batkovic camp and he was finally released on the 26th of December of 1995. Your Honours that concludes my summary and I have some further questions for the witness. If I may ask for the first question to be in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Sir, in your testimony in the Krstic case, as I've referred to just now in the summary, you referred to the enemy soldiers as Serb soldiers. Can you be more specific about where these soldiers were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: From Bosnia, they were Bosnians.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: So members of the Bosnian Serb army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you a few questions about Batkovic camp, please. In your prior testimony, you said that you were taken from Karakaj to the Batkovic camp. Where is the camp, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: In Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And I'd like to show you a map, please, and see if you can confirm the general location to help us in this courtroom with our orientation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: If I could have Exhibit P104, which is the Prosecution's map book, and at page 10 in e-court of that exhibit, please. If we could perhaps zoom in on the top two-thirds of the map, if possible, so cutting off just below the red circle. That's great, thank you. Sir, on this map we can see a portion of Eastern Bosnia in very simplified form, and I think we can just see at the bottom right-hand corner Bratunac, and then following up the river to the north, Zvornik and onwards to Bijeljina. Right at the top there is a red triangle marked as Batkovic camp. Does that location correspond roughly with where you believe Batkovic camp to be?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall around what date you arrived at Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: The 26th.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And of which month, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And what happened when you arrived at the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: The Red Cross was there already, and I was immediately registered with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Can I ask, please, to see 65 ter number 2686? Sir, this is an aerial photograph that we are looking at. Do you recognise any of the buildings as the buildings you knew at Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you, if I may, that the witness could mark this image.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And could we have an assistant to set up the magic pen, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Sir, the pen you're being given can be used to mark on the screen, and in a moment I'll ask you to mark some of the locations, if you recall them. If you make a mistake, then that can be erased. Now, first of all, where were you registered by the Red Cross when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Sir, you've drawn a red circle on the screen. Could you mark a number 1 next to that, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And was there some kind of facility where the Red Cross registered you or was this simply in the open air?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Well, it was a sort of a small tent.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Can you see on this picture the place where you were imprisoned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Could you mark that, please, with an X?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And perhaps put the number 2 next to it, just to be sure.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Sir, during the time you were at Batkovic camp, were there any other prisoners held with you in the building you've just marked?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And during your time in the camp, how many prisoners were held in that building?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I think about 200 prisoners. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Were these other prisoners already at the camp when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Did any more prisoners continue to arrive after you came to the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes, two or three of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And while you were at the camp, did you find out where the other prisoners were from?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I think two of them were brought from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Were they Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Who were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And of the 200 prisoners, were those Muslims or Serbs or a mixture? Can you explain?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Muslims from which area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Did you learn where these other Muslims from Srebrenica had been taken prisoner before they had been brought to the Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Well, I think that they used to be in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Had any of those prisoners been brought to the camp directly from Srebrenica or Potocari just after the Srebrenica enclave had been captured by the Bosnian Serb forces?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Now, sir, you've marked the building at the bottom of the picture. Do you know what the other buildings in this picture were used for?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: For example, were you taken to any separate building to eat or to work?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And while you were at the camp, did you find out whether there were any prisoners in the other buildings we can see on this picture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: When did you finally leave Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: On the 26th of December 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Sir, I don't have any further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: But I'd like to ask for this image to be tendered as an exhibit marked in court. I don't know if Your Honours would like any further information to be placed on the image by the witness or whether it's sufficient with the markings he has.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This aerial photograph with the markings will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document shall be assigned Exhibit P1765. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: And Your Honours, I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Elderkin. Sir, now the accused, Mr. Tolimir, is commencing his cross-examination. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. May there be peace in this house. May God's will be done in these proceedings and not mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Good morning to the witness. I wish him a pleasant stay here and a safe journey home. Since it's going to be difficult for me to gauge which of the details the witness does not want to go public with, we would kindly ask the witness and his legal counsel to pay attention to that and to caution me as soon as such a moment may arise. And since we speak the same language -- oh, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I do apologise as well and simply for the record I'd like to make clear that the Prosecution is not the witness's legal counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you for this comment, otherwise I would have done that. Please continue, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Elderkin. I apologise. I spoke automatically, without thinking. May the witness speak slowly and mind the need for a break between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Since what we are saying is going to be interpreted, please mind the cursor that you can see on the screen, and as soon as you see it stop, then start answering the question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we call up 1D558 in e-court, please? It is the witness's statement given to the OTP on the 23rd of May 1996. Thank you. We can see the statement now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question has to do with your statement. In the first paragraph of your statement, which can be found on the next page --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- just for a moment, this should not be broadcast. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And especially, perhaps Mr. Tolimir just misspoke. I don't see it any more. I heard something about the location where the witness is living now. But this can't be in public session. We will redact that part. Please continue, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please, you tell me what it is that you can say in public in answer to my question rather than me making that choice for you. Please state your mind in that respect whenever I put a question to you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I'd ask that we go into private session right now, please, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Private.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us who your commander was at a time when you were in the army until 1993? Can you tell us, if need be, in private session?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Zulfo was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us why was UNPROFOR banned from going into certain areas within the area of your brigade, if you know? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I know that they were -- there was no ban. They were free to go wherever they wanted to.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: So there was no area where movement was restricted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Tell us: In the area of responsibility and deployment of your brigade, was any -- were any weapons or ammunition manufactured?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about the ties between the Srebrenica area and Zepa area across the territory held by your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you participate in any of the actions under the command of the commander you just named?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you leave Srebrenica in order to carry out any military actions until 1993?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Which platoon were you a part of in -- up until 1993, or if you can tell us what the name of that unit was, if need be in private session?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was your brigade organised in squads, companies, platoons? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you go to man the lines of your own initiative or was it on the orders of your commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Well, we would normally go to man the lines in the evenings.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. After 1993, did any of you go to man the lines or to attend to any tasks that the unit might have had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did the Ministry of the Interior guard the boundaries of the demilitarised zone of Srebrenica or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you know who it was that the international forces of UNPROFOR were separating along the boundaries of the zone? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you know Mr. Ramiz Becirovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I did hear of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you know him or did you only hear of him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I only heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us if he was a member of the units stationed at Suceska? Was he a commander of the Territorial Defence there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have D120 shown now? D120, page 6 in Serbian and 10 in English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, could you please indicate for the record which document it is we are looking at?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We are looking at a document which was made at a time when he was a soldier in Srebrenica. It's a guide to Srebrenica, listing what the activities or duties of each of the units there was. We've already looked at the document. It was a contribution to a chronicle produced by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and it was that army which provided the information contained in this guide. So I'd like the witness to go through the document so that we may see the extent of his knowledge since he didn't know anything of the information I sought earlier.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I understand your position. On the other hand, this witness hasn't seen this in court and we just start at page 6, so it is necessary to explain what is about you are talking -- asking the witness. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I need another clarification. I was told this document is under seal, it should not be broadcast. And if there is still a reason that this document is under seal, you should be aware of that during your examination. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I've already stated for the record, but let me repeat that it was a contribution to a chronicle issued by the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina containing information about its units, and I'm going to ask the witness about the unit he was a member of.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Well, I don't know anything about any of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. This is my question: Do you see before you the roman numeral 3, and below it, the title, which reads, and it's page 9 in English, "Full Establishment of the Unit." So do you see here a mention of the unit you were a member of?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Perhaps you misunderstood my question. Does it not say beneath, three numbers and then the name of a brigade? Was this not the brigade you belonged to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you then tell us what was the base of your brigade? What was the name of your brigade?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And what was the name of your unit that was stationed in that location you mentioned which I will not name here? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: It was Territorial Defence. It was no unit. It was just --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you a member of that unit as of the 1st of May 1992? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Which unit?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: The one whose name I can see below the roman numeral 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you remember anything at all about the unit you belonged to at a time you were a soldier of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina in 1992? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember any operation carried out by your unit in 1992 and 1993? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did your unit take part in any action or operation, in any combat? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Does that mean that you only guarded your homes and went to join the unit as called up? Or did you just go to the units on your own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Well, we just guarded the homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And while you were on the lines -- my apologies to the interpreter. While you were manning the lines, can you tell me something about what your typical day would look like? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Well, you would spend the whole day in the trench, and that's what it looked like. What else can I tell you?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please tell the Trial Chamber of any activity or any mission of your unit or anything that you can recall while you were within the unit, even if you can tell us an anecdote or a story?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Well, as I've already told you, we just held the line, and that's about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you read what it said under the roman numeral 3 a moment ago, while you were looking at the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Well, could you recognise anything there, any activity, any person or any operation that is mentioned here as something that was carried out by the BH Army while you were a member of one of its units?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Throughout that period between 1992 through May 1993, were you a soldier? Were you wounded? Were you ill? Did you for any reason -- were you for any reason absent from within the unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Is there any reason why you're refusing to answer my questions, why you're refusing to say anything about your unit? Because we need it for the record and for the Trial Chamber, and perhaps you can tell us just the name of your commander, komandir, or can you tell us anything about the resupplies of the unit or anything of that sort?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: What do you mean resupply?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Well, can you tell us --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I would object to characterising the witness as refusing to answer the question. As far as I can see from the transcript, he's answered every single question he's been asked. In particular, also General Tolimir referred to the text he had on the screen and asked the witness whether he had a chance to read what was beneath the roman numeral, although he only directed his question to concern the first couple of lines after that roman numeral. If it's important for the witness to read the entire page, he should be given that opportunity because there is a fair amount of detail in there, but as I say, it's not -- I think it's objectionable for General Tolimir to characterise the witness as being a difficult witness who is refusing to answer. He certainly isn't doing that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We note that the witness was answering questions, however in a very short manner, and it is up to the Chamber to give weight to the kind of questions and answers. But indeed, the text below number 3 is a very long text, and if you want to put details to the witness, Mr. Tolimir, you should draw his attention to a specific part of that. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, and I would like to thank you Mr. Elderkin for making this remark regarding my questioning. I have no further questions for the witness about this text and it is not my intention to ask him to study this document. He has better things to do. Now I will move on to some other issues and perhaps then he can answer my questions. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see 1D565 in e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This is a statement provided by you, Mr. Witness, on the 20th of July 1996, to the state commission for gathering facts on war crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, this document -- a document with this number is not in your list and perhaps you misspoke. Please check that again. Mr. Elderkin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Furthermore, if the document does show up on the list and it is what General Tolimir described it as, it shouldn't be broadcast obviously.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies to e-court. I misquoted the number. I should have asked for 1D562 rather than 1D565. So could we please pull up 1D562? Thank you. And, again, let me repeat (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This document should not be broadcast. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you see this document, witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Is this document indeed a statement that you provided to the bodies which we can see in the heading, in the upper left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Why didn't you mention in this statement that you were a member of the army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: [No verbal response]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you had occasion to read through this statement during your earlier testimonies or earlier preparations for the statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Have you ever seen it after you've provided it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Would you need to read it before I can put some questions to you? Because I'd like to go through this statement of yours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Well, I don't think it's necessary for me to read it through again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have a problem again. You are overlapping, both speakers, and it's difficult for the interpreters to catch everything. Mr. Elderkin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, given the reference to the exact date of the statement and to whom it was given, which is as far as I just saw page 24 lines 1 to 2 in LiveNote, I'd ask for that information to be redacted. I don't know if this document is available elsewhere publicly and could be more easily linked to the witness's identity as a result.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is this document under seal? Is it a confidential document?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: If it were to be admitted, I would ask for it to be under seal, but I don't know where else it exist, whether -- for example, in the country where it was originally taken, for example, it might be accessible publicly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We will redact these lines. Please go ahead, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I don't know if I'm permitted to mention place names or should I just skip over it and would you then admit this document in view of the fact that everything will be redacted? In other words, I don't know how to put questions to this witness if he's unwilling to read it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I've already said that I was a member of the army and what I did while I was its member and there is nothing else I can add, and the statement that I provided was brief. I did not provide the full statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I don't see a reason to say that the witness is not willing to read this document. It is still under discussion and you asked the Chamber how to proceed. I think if there is a link between the witness, in person, and a specific place, then we altogether should be very careful with that. On the other hand, it's no problem to mention certain locations like Srebrenica because everybody knows that we are dealing with events in Srebrenica. So we should decide case by case. Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I only said this because the witness said that he hadn't read this statement, either during the proofing for this testimony or for the earlier testimonies, and that he hadn't read it since he actually made the statement. So I've asked him whether it was necessary for him to read it now, to refresh his memory, but since he said that it wasn't, could we then see the next page of this statement, please? That's page 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I ask the witness, do you recall this statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A little bit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But you recall that you have given this statement at an earlier time, years ago?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, years ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please continue, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, would you please take a look at the second paragraph on page 2 of this statement? And I'm referring to the Serbian version, where you say that in a village, and I won't mention the name of the village: "I saw a large number of assembled soldiers and civilians. I think that there may have been about 15.000 people there. I arrived there on the 15th [as interpreted] of July 1995, and on the evening of that day, part of the soldiers and civilians went towards Kamenica Pobudjansko." My apologies, would you please redact this. Well, they went in the direction that you mention here? So my question based on this is what soldiers are you referring to here and which civilians are you referring to? Who was going, whatever you are saying that they were going in this statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Well, the civilians were from Srebrenica. As for soldiers, I don't know what soldiers these were. I can't remember that part.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. But are these your words? Can you recall that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Just one correction. I see at page 27, line 9 a reference to the 15th of July, which I think should be the 11th of July as it appears in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: That's correct. Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell me whether there is a possibility that this statement was actually compiled after you provided it and just trying to recapture your words?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Are you sure of any portion of the text that you had occasion to read so far, that these were in fact your words?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you tell us, please, whether, when you provided the statement, you signed, you placed your signature on each page of the text that was typed out after you've given the statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I'm not even sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please look at the bottom of this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We need the bottom of both pages, especially in B/C/S, full to the bottom. Yes, thank you. Witness, can you see a handwritten name? Is it yours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you recall having signed this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I did not hear the witness's answer. Could he please repeat it? You asked him whether he had signed this document and he said that he hadn't.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did sign it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Oh, you did, thank you. So does that mean that what is contained therein are, in fact, your words?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Well, most probably but I can't recall every detail. I can't recall mentioning all of these details.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you state before investigating organs that there had been an order for all able-bodied men from your town to go to the place which was mentioned a moment ago, Jaglici, and that civilians were supposed to go to Potocari? Was this your statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Well, I heard that from other people, and we did go to Jaglici. So there was an instruction to go to Jaglici, whereas women and children were supposed to go to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we now please see 1D558 in e-court? And perhaps we can hear from the witness whether he can recall this document at least.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, are you tendering the document, 1D562?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Yes. I would like to tender it, because we will also revisit this document if the witness mentions any of the events that are contained therein. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received under seal and the next document should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, 65 ter document 1D562 shall be assigned Exhibit D151, admitted under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: In front of us we have your statement given under -- oh, no, it's your birthday -- no. You gave the statement on the 23rd of May 1996. This statement was given to the International Criminal Tribunal for the Prosecution of persons. My question is: Did you talk to the investigators of the ICTY on the 23rd of May 1996?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I don't remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Take a look at the second page of your statement. Thank you. Now, if we take a look at the second paragraph on the screen, fourth line, where you say: "There was an order that all able-bodied men should go to Jaglici and women and children to go to Potocari." My question is as follows: Did you state this while you were giving this statement to the investigators of ICTY?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us who gave this order? What authorities gave this order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I don't know that. I already told you that I heard from other people that there was such an order, who gave it, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Yes, but here in the statement you didn't say that you heard it from others. Here you simply said the order came for all able-bodied men to go to Jaglici and line up and women and children to go to Potocari.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Who gave this order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I heard it from other people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: So did you obey what you heard from other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: So was that a normal way of issuing orders, people tell that to other people?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: So you didn't have a normal system of disseminating information via couriers and others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Well, we had many people from your place who would say, well, that a courier arrived and then informed them about what to do. Is that something that also happened in your village?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I simply said what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: If an order came that all able-bodied men should go to Jaglici, does that mean that this order was issued by the military organs in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I don't know. It's possible. I heard it from others. I did not hear it from some military personnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And when you arrived to that place where you were ordered to come and line up, did somebody speak to you then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you arrive there with your arms or without it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Without the arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Does that mean that everybody was unarmed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: As far as I could see around me, nobody was armed. Whether everybody was unarmed, that I cannot tell.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you see any commander, maybe a commander from your unit or any other commander?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you go there individually, on foot, from your village or did you go with other men who comprised your unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I went with two or three other men. It wasn't an organised movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you have a family that went to Potocari in line with this oral order?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Does that mean that you received the order to go where you went and the women received the order to go where they went?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how you could interpret that but that's what was told to us. Women to Potocari; men to Jaglici. That's what I heard and that's what was done.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: So if something would happen to one of those who obeyed the order to go where the men were ordered to go, does that mean that such a person would have a right to request some compensation because it was a military task to go there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: What kind of military task?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: But who can issue such an order? Can such an order be issued by somebody who is not authorised to give it, or can such an order be given only by a person authorised to issue such orders?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I don't know who can issue orders. We were simply trying to save our skins at the time. We simply wanted to hide in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I asked you already, and I'm asking you once again, are you willing to answer my questions or not? It's not about me. I don't need that. We are talking here about the Trial Chamber. They have to see what happened. You don't have to feel obligated towards me.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I am answering the questions to the best of my ability.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To be very clear, you need these answers, as everybody else, like the Prosecution and the Chamber. This is the reason why the witness is here. Mr. Elderkin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Again, I'd say the question is objectionable. I can't see any basis on which to accuse the witness of not giving an answer. He seems to have, again, given a clear answer in some detail and that can be followed up by further questions, if necessary, but to suggest again that he's trying not to answer is unfair on the witness and inappropriate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I don't want to repeat my comment on that. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Elderkin. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you now look in the middle of the statement? 23rd row of the second paragraph. Maybe we could somehow mark it on the screen for the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I suggest that you read this sentence so that everybody can pick out what you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. It goes as follows: "At least 200 people were killed by the ambush and they were left in that location." Maybe we could mark that part in e-court. And as I said, it's the 23rd line. Yeah, it's here: "At least 200 people were killed by the ambush. And they were left in that location. We took the wounded with us and began walking again for about half an hour. Then we were surrounded by Serbs again. They had come amongst us, taking people and killing them." Can we mark this part of the statement in e-court so that the witness can see exactly what my question is about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Witness, now you see the cursor and the screen. This is the part Mr. Tolimir is referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we maybe now put the cursor at the beginning of the sentence, "At least 200 people were killed." So -- yes, exactly, so that the witness can see it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: So now the cursor is exactly at the beginning of this sentence.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you say anything more about this event when 200 people were killed and left to lie there? Where exactly that happened, for instance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: We went through the woods and arrived to the village of Kamenica. We sat down in order to rest. However, Serbian soldiers ambushed us, surrounded us, and started shooting from various weapons, and that's where they killed those people. There were some wounded, we took them with us. However, they surrounded us again and shelled us. So the wounded were left where they were because everybody simply ran wherever they could into the woods. You want to know something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell the Trial Chamber whether you know those people, were they later buried? That location, was it somehow marked by anybody, maybe some international organs? Were you maybe later taken to that location? Can you tell us what was done with those victims? Where are they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I know nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, can we go back to 1D562? That's the statement by this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is now D151 under seal and should not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we have page 2 of this statement? It describes similar events, so I want to see whether the witness will be able to remember these events now, when he takes a look at the statement given to the organs of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now can you take a look at the third paragraph, which begins with, "As we made our way..." When you read this paragraph, let me know and then I'm going to pose my question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is as follows: Where did you see these 300 killed and a large number of wounded people, was it on the same axis? And what is the distance between this spot and the first spot that you described?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I think that all this was generally speaking from Jaglici all the way down there, that there were about 300 killed people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. However, for these proceedings, it would be very important if you could tell us whether everything happened in one location or they were killed all the way along the road because if you look here, you said: "The Chetniks surrounded us and opened fire on us, killing over 300 people and wounding a large number. We were in disarray as both soldiers and civilians fled wherever they could, while the wounded were left behind on the path." So here in this statement, you say very precisely that it was on some sort of path. So can you tell us, where exactly did that happen, where exactly were 300 people killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I said when we went through the words from Jaglici towards Kamenica and then there was about 200 people and then also down there when they shelled us near Pobudje.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Does that mean that 500 people were killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No, no, no. No, in total around 300 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: After this event that you describe here in the third paragraph, did you see any other place where there were killings and casualties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In the last sentence of this paragraph, the third paragraph, you say: "We were in disarray as both soldiers and civilians fled wherever they could, while the wounded were left behind on the path." Can you tell us what soldiers were they? Did you see any soldiers there? What soldiers were running away? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Were they maybe the soldiers of the army of the Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina from the same place where you were there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: It's possible. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, can you take a look at the second paragraph, right above, where in the second sentence -- no, actually in the first sentence, you say: "When I came to such and such village, I saw a large number of assembled soldiers and civilians. I think there may have been about 15.000 people." My question is as follows: Can you remember now whether there, at the assembly place, you saw any soldier -- soldiers of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No. I saw people. There were some people in camouflage uniforms. But I didn't see anybody wearing -- bearing any arms. That's what I meant when I said that there were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that you saw some people in uniform but you didn't see any weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't know exactly how many.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: After the VRS entered Srebrenica, did your army withdraw from that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: What army?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: The army that had been in Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: How could an army be there if it was a save zone?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I'm simply asking you and you should answer.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: All right. You yourself said that there was a large number of soldiers and civilians. Can we take a look at another document? Maybe it would -- it should remind you that there were some soldiers.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I said that I saw people in camouflage uniforms. I don't know how many of them, and I did not see any weapons.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Can we now take a look at 1D373?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, before we move to another document, we must have our first break now. But before we break, I would like ask the witness only one question: What was your rank in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina as a soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't have any rank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You were a simple soldier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, may I ask that the witness be given his statements? Because we will continue discussing those after the break. It would be a good thing for him to have a look at it, at all the statements, over the break, unless he has them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think -- Mr. Elderkin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: I'm afraid it may take the entire break to call up the statements all in B/C/S and hand them to the witness. I do have some copies in English. I know the witness does have some fluency in English, but I would imagine if the questioning will be in B/C/S it would be preferable for all concerned that he review them in that language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is it possible to print the B/C/S version and to give it to the witness? I was told by the registrar that this is possible. Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. If necessary, we can provide the copies that the OTP gave us. It takes only a couple of minutes to have them copied and that would facilitate the work for all of us. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think the most practical way is that the registrar print it and give it to the witness, but you should tell us which documents you will use during the further examination. Tell us just the numbers and the registrar will provide the witness with the documents.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. 1D558, 1D559, and what we have on our screens, D561. So if those three documents could be copied and given to the witness over the break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Elderkin?

utterances.speaker: MR. ELDERKIN
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's quite some reading to get through during the break. I don't know how the witness is feeling, but it's been going quite fast this morning and perhaps the break could be extended slightly so he has time to both read and also relax slightly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think is a good recommendation. We will have our first break now and resume 15 minutes past 11. Thank you very much. And during the break, the Chamber would be -- would appreciate if you could read these statements in your own language. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to give notice that the next break will be a little earlier than usual, quarter past 12, because I personally have another commitment. I have to take part in a meeting and therefore the last session of today will be pursuant to Rule 15 bis, without my presence. Sir, did you have the opportunity to read through the documents in your language you were provided with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Presiding Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, have you been given the three statements you gave to the BH authorities and the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Are they authentic statements in terms of their contents? Is that what you said? And do they all contain your signature?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Well, can you tell us which of the statements is not authentic in terms of what you were saying at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Well, when I said no, I didn't mean that they weren't authentic. I meant that not all of them had my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us which one doesn't have your signature?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can 1D558 be shown in e-court to see whether it has a signature?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think again, the three statements shouldn't be broadcast. We see in the -- to shorten the procedure in the B/C/S version we don't see a signature, but in the English translation we see a handwriting on the bottom of the page, but we have to state again the witness was provided with the B/C/S versions of the three statements. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: As we can see, the statements you gave about the events which transpired during the attempt to break out of Srebrenica in the direction of Tuzla, they have been signed, have they not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And are they authentic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I tender these three statements which are authentic according to the witness, be admitted -- I wish to tender them into evidence. That's 1D558, 1D559.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: 1D558 and 1D559 will be admitted into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, these documents shall be assigned the following exhibits numbers, 65 ter document 1D558 shall be assigned Exhibit D152, admitted under seal. 65 ter document 1D559 shall be assigned Exhibit D153, admitted under seal. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: The last question put to you was by Their Honours concerning your rank and your answer was that you were just an ordinary soldier. Before that, I asked you if you had seen any soldiers and your answer was that you only saw people in uniform but without any weapons.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we -- can we now have 1D373 shown? There we will see what the commander of the army has to say about whether there were any armed soldiers in the column. This is 1D373. The heading states, "Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, BH Army, 3rd Corps command," et cetera and it's a report on the situation in Srebrenica. So, in other words, it's a document issued by the 3rd Corps, and can we turn to the next page, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We should state that the date is the 16th of July 1995. There is no translation yet, English translation. We have only the B/C/S version on the screen. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. That's right. The document was written on the 16th, precisely at a time when there was a breakthrough which was on the earlier day, and on the 16th, the corridor was opened, as stated by the witness who was here yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, this document was produced and you will see this at the bottom where we have another heading, again stating the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Main Staff of the army, the date is the 16th of July 1995, and it states: "Report on the Situation in Srebrenica." So what this means is that the document, the heading of which we were quoting a moment ago, was basically compiled on the basis of this here document; that's to say, a document issued by the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now go to page 4 so that the witness may see the signature block?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: You can see that the document was signed by the commander of the army, General Rasim Delic, and we have here the certification of transcription of the copy.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back to page 3 now?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I will read out a portion of the document issued by Rasim Delic. And let me tell you that there is nothing for you to hide because this is a document that was given to us by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I have nothing to hide.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Since you said that you didn't see any soldiers in the column, this is what Delic says. Let's read from item 3, page 3, item 3 at the bottom of the page. It's been marked for you there. And I'm quoting: "The units of the 28th Division --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Page 3, item 3 of the order issued by Rasim Delic on the 16th, or, rather, it's a reports on the situation in Srebrenica: "The units of the 28th Division of the ground forces have been pulling out of Srebrenica, or rather have been fighting their way out of Srebrenica. The units of the 28th Division had remained compact. They have been successful in their activities on the temporarily occupied territory. They have been inflicting great losses on the aggressor. They have so far captured eight Chetniks alive. The units of the 28th Division have linked up with the units of the 2nd Corps. They continue fighting jointly on the temporarily occupied territory. These units are expected to fully link up soon. The activities aim at taking advantage of the success achieved in the breakthrough."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This report was signed by General Rasim Delic, who was Chief of the General Staff of the BH Army at the time. Army General Rasim Delic. He says, in item 3, that a breakthrough took place, that there were units deployed to the territory of Republika Srpska, and that they are successful in their fighting, et cetera. So my question is: What were they fighting with, if the only thing you saw was soldiers in uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Well, what I'd like to know is where this fighting was taking place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I can tell you that the fighting was taking place in the sector of Baljkovica, this is something that several witnesses testified to. Here, there are two commanders, the commander of the corps, brigadier Sackim -- Sakib Mahmuljin, the commander of the 3rd Corps reports on this in his document and attaches to his report a report written by the army General Rasim Delic. I've told you -- I've read just now what it is that they said. I cannot provide you with any further information. I'm not allowed to under the rules. So I'm going to ask you this, and then Their Honours will be the ones to say whether there was fighting. Could there have been civilians as part of the forces attempting a breakthrough?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you this: There may have been armed individuals among them but I didn't see them. I was leaving the area on the following day, and I was captured already on the 13th, so I really have no knowledge about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us in which part of the column were you as you set out from Jaglici? Were you at the head or at the rear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: At the rear.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: At the rear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us who was securing the rear of the column? Was it the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: I didn't see anyone securing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you know if the Mountain Battalion was at the rear of the column protecting the column moving from Srebrenica in the direction of Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us, did you see any senior officers, as you set out from Jaglici, anyone whom you knew to have been commanding or senior officer?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us, did you see your commander, Zulfo in Jaglici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: No, I think he had gone earlier on, he had left earlier on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Very well. I will not be asking you things you know nothing about. I read this out to you so that you would learn that there were others who had other sort of information, but there is no need for us to debate the issue. Let's move to another topic you are willing to discuss. You say that over 300 civilians and soldiers were killed, along the way as you came upon an ambush. Can you tell us how you came upon the ambush and what happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: As I set out from Jaglici on the following day, I don't know at which time, the Serbian soldiers started opening fire on us from the surrounding hills. We went through a wooded area, a great many people were killed by gunfire. As we reached the village of Kamenica, we stopped there for -- to get a minute's rest, but all of a sudden we came under fire. There were a lot of people killed on this occasion. We took along all the wounded. Then shelling and gunfire started again. At that point we dispersed, fleeing for our lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. So the location where there were these many people wounded or killed was Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes, from Jaglici all the way to Kamenica and on to Kasaba.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did the column come under fire in Kamenica for the first time or was it already under fire in Jaglici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: It was in Jaglici that we first came under fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement which we will look at now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is D51 now, can we have it shown, you've signed it -- I'm sorry, it's D151. Thank you, Aleksandar. We can see page 2 of the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Let's look at the third paragraph that I just referred to where you said that there were over 300 people killed. And then, in paragraph 4, you go on to say: "I was in a group of ten of us, including so and so, and we set out from Srebrenica to Kamenica. On the way there we came across a civilian," and that's where you were taken prisoner by the Chetniks. Now, did I quote your words accurately?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Is there anything you would like to add to this? What happened to you? What became of you when you were captured? Where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: We tried to cross the road but we were surrounded by the Serbian soldiers and taken prisoner there. One of us had a pistol on him, which was seized from him. They took a rucksack that we had, and then they took us to the school building in Kasaba. We had to put our hands behind our heads and that's how we got there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you spend the night in the school building in Kasaba and were you detained there? Were you told that you were going to be kept as prisoners?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes, but we didn't spend the night there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Very well. What happened next? Can you tell Their Honours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: At that point, we were taken back to the football pitch there, where there was a crowd of prisoners already. There were quite a few Serbian soldiers. The captives were told to sit in rows. Serbian soldiers surrounded the pitch. There were two APCs up there on the road. Mladic arrived too. He addressed us. He told us that there is a hundred defence lines between there and Tuzla and that not even a bird would be able to pass through.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. Now let us take a look at your statement, 1D558, where you speak about this, and at the very start you say -- or, rather, at the beginning of page 2, you mention this event, so I will put a question to you while allowing you to just take a look, to jog your memory, to take a look at this statement.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, we should not publish this because there is information on this page pointing to the identity of the witness. So we have page 1 of the statement before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We can see here the portion where you mention Mladic. That's in the last three lines.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please scroll this statement up so the witness can see that portion? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, witness, can you see in line 3 from the bottom, where you say, and that's on the next page in the English version: "Other people arrived as well, including some wounded people who were then treated by the Serbs. Some of these men were separated and put in a separate group on the pitch. We all sat there. And after about an hour of my arrival General Ratko Mladic arrived." So my question is do you recall if that was in the morning or the afternoon of that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: It was in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, I'm asking you this because you say at one point here, at 1400 hours, so this could have been at around 1500 hours or 3.00 p.m.; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-016
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now show the witness the following page of the statement so that the witness can read parts of his own statement?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Here we have it where you talk about Mladic arriving, that he came in a jeep: "... and I believe that he was dressed in a uniform.
